top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards one idea with a clean two-person allocation: at the magic wavelength the clock-transition light shift cancels, so many neutral atoms sit in the Lamb-Dicke regime with Doppler and recoil shifts suppressed and projection noise reduced by atom number. This is distinct from the 2005 comb and the 2012 single-ion control, has been reproduced by independent laboratories agreeing near 1e-18, and has already yielded measured physics (gravitational redshift over centimetres, many-body clock shifts, bounds on drifting constants). Katori (concept and first demonstration) and Ye (record realisation) map onto the citation. IceCube (P002) is a genuine and unexpected discovery, which I value, but confirmation is within one detector, source identification is still early, and it is a lower maturity and a less settled attribution; I still prefer it to no award.
recusal_note: Field proximity only: I am an atomic theorist who works on precision atomic structure and have close ties to the attosecond community, but no apparent collaboration with Katori, Ye or the IceCube authors; none apparent from profile for a required recusal.
